companionBriefing: Portia only lets in people who greet her properly. Answer in Italian; mixing in English is fine while you learn.
Tap a word under her line to see what it means, or Translate sentence for the whole line. On her newest line each one uses a hint from my allowance.
The words and phrases shown beneath her lines go into your Spellbook, where you can review them later.

lines.native: Buongiorno. I am Portia. A greeting and your name, please. Entry requires manners; structural integrity is optional.
lines.translation: Good morning. I am Portia. A greeting and your name, please. Entry requires manners; structural integrity is optional.
lines.narrative: A visitors’ book slides from the archway’s keystone. Apparently, even crumbling markets have reception.

lines.native: Ciao! Greeting accepted. Now, come ti chiami? Your name, please; an exclamation mark is not a legal identity.
lines.translation: Hi! Greeting accepted. Now, what is your name? Your name, please; an exclamation mark is not a legal identity.
lines.narrative: A visitors’ book slides out of Portia’s keystone. The name column remains pointedly empty.

lines.native: Piacere, Sam! Bene, il tuo nome è qui. Your introduction is accepted. And now, any curiosity about your host? Courtesy is a two-way archway.
lines.translation: Pleased to meet you, Sam! Good, your name is here. Your introduction is accepted. And now, any curiosity about your host? Courtesy is a two-way archway.
lines.narrative: A visitors’ book slides out of Portia’s keystone. She records Sam with the solemnity usually reserved for disputed borders.

lines.native: Io? Mi chiamo Portia. Piacere, Sam! You asked me back. Excellent manners. Slightly overwhelming. Benvenuto! You may enter; I shall record this as a good day.
lines.translation: Me? My name is Portia. Nice to meet you, Sam! You asked me back. Excellent manners. Slightly overwhelming. Welcome! You may enter; I shall record this as a good day.
lines.narrative: Portia’s visitors’ book snaps shut in her keystone. Someone has asked about her. The paperwork has not prepared her for this.
